Short lessons you fly in MSFS while Trade Winds watches and coaches. With the sim connected, each step ticks itself off when you actually do it. Every lesson pays $150 toward your career.

Set up your controls

Engine start and taxi

Taxiing is where the flight starts.

10 min

Your first takeoff

A good takeoff is smooth and boring: full power, straight down the centerline, lift off at the right speed, climb at the best rate..

10 min

Straight, level and trimmed

Trim takes the pressure off the controls so the plane flies itself.

10 min

Turns without losing altitude

In a turn, part of the wing's lift tilts sideways, so the nose wants to drop.

10 min
⛽

Mixture: what the co-pilot keeps telling you

Air gets thinner as you climb.

8 min
🪶

Flaps and speed limits

Flaps let you fly slower and descend steeper, but they have speed limits.

10 min
⚠️

Lesson 8 · Intermediate

Slow flight and stalls

A stall isn't the engine stopping.

12 min
⬜

Fly the traffic pattern

15 min

The landing

Good landings come from good approaches.

15 min

Lesson 11 · Advanced

Crosswind landing

Autopilot basics

Autopilot is a tool for managing workload, not a replacement for flying.

8 min

Talking to ATC in MSFS

10 min

From sim to sky: becoming a pilot

Everything you just practiced is real.

5 min

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.

Live sim off

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.
